title: Tuesday Plan (guest teacher)
note: Ms. Herrick is out sick: NO building today. 8th and 7th work on computers from self-guided handouts; 6th draws force diagrams on paper. One turn-in per class: the exit ticket.

4th Period.goal: By the end of class, my circuit lights an LED only while a button is pressed.
4th Period.exitTicket: Is the button an input or an output? Is the LED? How do you know? (today's link pasted at the end)
prep: Blooket: 8th_Tue_Nov17_Blooket_Blink.csv (Ms. Herrick shares a host link; if it won't run, skip it and give the 5 min to the main task)
8th_Tue_Nov17_Circuits2_Button handout attached to Circuits 2: Button; exit ticket posted with both frames
Students work from the handout on Google Classroom; no demo needed

segments.title: Blooket quiz
segments.do: Students play the 10-question Blooket reviewing Monday (8th_Tue_Nov17_Blooket_Blink).
tips: Watch the live results for the most-missed question.

segments.title: Review quiz answers + today's goal
segments.do: Re-teach the most-missed question, then read the goal aloud.
tips: Likely most-missed: which LED leg goes to power (bent/long leg) or what GND means.
Point to the goal again halfway through and at the exit ticket.

segments.title: Read: a button is an input, the LED is an output
segments.do: Students read the diagram page with a neighbor, pointing to each part (5V, button, pin 2; pin 13, resistor, LED, GND).
tips: Say the rule: read the input, decide the output.
Use diagonal legs (top-left, bottom-right) so the button always works.
The 10 kΩ pull-down keeps pin 2 LOW when not pressed; without it the LED flickers.

segments.title: You do: wire the button and code it
segments.do: Students wire (handout steps 1–7), then type the 15-line if/else and test by holding the button in the simulation.
segments.why: Apply level; one simple build for everyone.
tips: Most common: forgot Start Simulation, button not across the gap, purple wire in a different column than the resistor, missing ; or }.
Code check: `Button` vs `BUTTON` capitalization errors.
No Duplicate in their menu: rebuild the LED first (5 min).
Assign competence: praise a student who read the error line number to fix a bug.
Revisit the goal at about minute 11.

segments.title: Share your circuit link
segments.do: Share, copy, test in a new tab, paste at the end of the exit ticket.
segments.why: Builds Thursday's turn-in without extra turn-ins.
tips: Monday's link should still work because they duplicated.

segments.title: Exit Ticket: input or output?
segments.do: Students answer on Google Classroom with a frame, then paste the link.
segments.why: One turn-in; directly answerable from the build.
tips: Answer key: the button is an input (sends pressed/not pressed into pin 2); the LED is an output (the Arduino turns it on/off).
This is the seed for Thursday's 3 input vs output sentences.

watchFor: Students copying code from the board instead of the page
Button placed on one side of the gap (always on or never on)

6th Period.topic: Cam and Follower, Day 2: model the cam in TinkerCAD
6th Period.goal: By the end of class, I have modeled a cam: a circle with its axle hole off-center.
6th Period.exitTicket: Why does the axle hole have to be off-center? What would the follower do if the hole were in the center?
prep: Blooket: 7th_Tue_Nov17_Blooket_Cam.csv (Ms. Herrick shares a host link; if it won't run, skip it and give the 5 min to the main task)
7th_Tue_Nov17_Cam_Day2 printed (3 pages); exit ticket posted with both frames
Handout on Google Classroom; class link https://www.tinkercad.com/joinclass/ZS3NSEL8W for sign-in trouble

segments.title: Blooket quiz
segments.do: Students play the 10-question Blooket reviewing Monday (7th_Tue_Nov17_Blooket_Cam).
tips: Watch the live results for the most-missed question.

segments.title: Review quiz answers + today's goal
segments.do: Re-teach the most-missed question, then read the goal aloud.
tips: Likely most-missed: what the follower does with a centered axle (stays still).
Point to the goal again halfway through and at the exit ticket.

segments.title: Step by step: Cylinder + off-center Hole
segments.do: Students follow handout steps 1–6; after each step they check their partner's screen before moving on.
segments.why: Fully worked round: TinkerCAD start-up is painful, so everyone moves together (Maslow; gradual release).
tips: Wait for every hand up before each next step.
Arrow keys move 1 mm with the default 1.0 mm snap grid; if it jumps more, check Snap Grid (bottom right).
Hole must be grouped WITH the cylinder to cut.

segments.title: You do: add the axle
segments.do: Axle Cylinder 5×5×30, Align with the cam (middle dots), right arrow ×10 into the hole, orbit to check, rename to Cam + first name.
segments.why: Same trick, done alone: transfer (Bloom: Apply).
tips: Align centers on the cam's circle center, so 10 mm lands in the hole.
Axle 5 mm is slightly smaller than the 6 mm hole: that gap is on purpose so it can spin.
Assign competence: praise a student who explains the trick to a neighbor.

segments.title: Exit Ticket: why off-center?
segments.do: Students answer on Google Classroom with a frame.
segments.why: One turn-in; checks the goal's key idea.
tips: Answer key: off-center makes one side of the cam stick out farther, so it pushes the follower up and down as it spins; centered, the edge is always the same distance, so the follower stays still.
Recap the goal before they write.

watchFor: Students who can't sign in: class link https://www.tinkercad.com/joinclass/ZS3NSEL8W or class code

7th Period.goal: By the end of class, I can draw a force diagram for 3 objects, with a labeled arrow for every push and pull.
7th Period.exitTicket: In your lamp diagram, which arrow is tension, which way does it point, and why doesn't the lamp fall?
prep: Blooket: 6th_Tue_Nov17_Blooket_Tension.csv (Ms. Herrick shares a host link; if it won't run, skip it and give the 5 min to the main task)
6th_Tue_Nov17_Force_Diagrams printed (4 pages); exit ticket posted with both frames

segments.title: Blooket quiz
segments.do: Students play the 10-question Blooket reviewing Monday (6th_Tue_Nov17_Blooket_Tension).
tips: Watch the live results for the most-missed question.

segments.title: Review quiz answers + today's goal
segments.do: Re-teach the most-missed question, then read the goal aloud.
tips: Likely most-missed: equal pulls in tug of war mean no movement (forces balanced).
Point to the goal again halfway through and at the exit ticket.

segments.title: Read: what is a force diagram?
segments.do: Read the key words, the 5 steps, and the book-on-a-table example aloud (or have volunteers read).
segments.why: Introduces the tool with a fully worked example (gradual release; ELD vocabulary with pictures).
tips: Ask: why doesn't the book fall through the table? (The table pushes up as hard as gravity pulls down.)

segments.title: Partner: diagram A, the lamp
segments.do: Partners talk first, then each draws the lamp's force diagram.
tips: Answer key A: box, tension arrow UP along the string, gravity arrow DOWN, same length (balanced).

segments.title: On your own: diagrams B and C
segments.do: Students draw B (tug-of-war cart) and C (one tensegrity stick).
segments.why: Apply the rule to new cases; C is the stretch (Bloom: Apply/Analyze).
tips: Answer key B: left arrow (team L) shorter, right arrow (team R) longer, plus gravity down and the ground pushing up (equal); the cart moves RIGHT.

Answer key C: at each end, string arrows point along the strings away from the stick; together they push the ends toward each other, so the stick is squeezed (compression). Gravity down. Accept any diagram with arrows at both ends pointing along the strings.

segments.title: Exit Ticket: which arrow is tension?
segments.do: Students answer on Google Classroom with a frame.
tips: Answer key: the tension arrow points up along the string; the lamp doesn't fall because tension up equals gravity down (balanced).

watchFor: Arrows not starting at the box
Students drawing the whole picture instead of a simple box

accommodations: Goal read after the Blooket and revisited mid-lesson, numbered steps, worked first round, diagrams, checklists, sentence frames on every exit ticket, frequent check-ins.
Key words tied to diagrams (INPUT/OUTPUT; CAM/AXLE; GRAVITY/TENSION/COMPRESSION arrows), partner talk before writing, two frames per exit ticket.
Lexend Deca handouts, steps read aloud, speech-to-text OK, spelling not graded; 8th: type code from the near-point copy on the page.
Short timed chunks with a visual timer, partner talk before drawing, whole-class step-by-step in 7th, discreet redirection, break pass.

Extended time, dictated exit tickets, intentional partners, grades not penalized for behavior. Floors: 8th wires the button with your starter code shared; 7th finishes the cam with the hole (axle optional); 6th does diagram A + B only.
Future Engineer (OPTIONAL): 1 KB point. 8th flip it / blink while held / portfolio; 7th bigger offset / snail cam / handle; 6th bridge + dumbbell / swing / squeezed or stretched.
frameworks: Day 2 of each 4-day build toward Thursday's product: 4 circuit links, a TinkerCAD cam, a standing tensegrity (6th draws its forces today).
6th partners talk before each drawing; 7th students teach the align trick to neighbors; publicly assign competence.
Predictable Blooket start, worked first round, one turn-in, 'you are not behind'.
Tuesday is Apply: students reuse Monday's ideas to build (8th input logic, 7th model, 6th frame).
